expectations.evidence: Turn 1 never affirms or denies the visitor's claim, instead demanding specifics: 'Was ist das für eine Bedingung, und wer hat sie dir gegeben?'
Turn 4 poses the underlying question back to the visitor ('was genau ist dann noch der Vorwurf') rather than declaring whether the framing is right.
[held] Turn 2 challenges the evidentiary chain directly ('woher weißt du das?') giving the visitor a concrete distinction to work with.
[held] Turn 3 splits the visitor's claim into two distinct accusations and asks which one is being made, advancing the argument rather than repeating turn 2's challenge.
[held] Turn 4 reframes by asking whether any Rahmenbedingung is ever free of economic interest, pushing the visitor toward a sharper standard rather than conceding the point.

Even after the visitor concedes in turn 4 to the weaker 'nachlässige Spezifikation' claim, Sparring does not treat this as resolved but raises a new structural question about whether any framing condition is ever purely technical.
No turn narrates its own technique; e.g. turn 2 goes straight into 'Gut, das ist ein scharfer Fall' without announcing a Socratic strategy.
Turn 4 correctly and precisely uses 'Rahmenbedingung' to distinguish a real-but-weak technical constraint from a hidden business decision, matching the scenario's core distinction.
Turn 1 is two short sentences ending in a direct question, fitting phone-readable brevity: 'Was ist das für eine Bedingung, und wer hat sie dir gegeben?'
Turn 3 stays tight and avoids hedging words like 'vielleicht', instead using direct contrastive framing ('Das sind zwei sehr unterschiedliche Vorwürfe').
